entries.axis_a: D1 V1 answers how work is carried, not who the organisation is (§1.1)
entries.axis_b: G1 The organisation is a set of configured positions

value.objective: O2 Jobs, not code paths — PM, coach, kata, development and operations are job_keys in one catalogue using the same card, run and approval primitives (D31, P6).

entries.axis_a: D2 The field builds agent conversations; organisations run on positions, work products, gates, baselines and evidence (§1.3)

value.objective: O3 Every decision is auditable — TOGAF, SAFe, PMP and MSP artefacts are rows, gates and evidence, and every decision row names its option, confidence and policy (D32, D30).

entries.axis_a: D3 A job is only as capable as what it may call (§11)
entries.axis_b: G3 Every tool a job may call is versioned, bound and ledgered

value.objective: O4 Every tool is governed — tool/toolkit versions, an effect ceiling per binding and one `tool_call` row per call (D41, D45).

entries.axis_a: D4 The v4 lesson: the right roles on the wrong substrate (§1.4)
entries.axis_b: G4 The system builds and operates itself

value.objective: O5 The conveyor develops and operates itself under its own gates — development projects change conveyor and its dependency repos through lane, PR, CI, review, merge, deploy and verify (D34, P7).

entries.axis_a: D5 Three independently built things arrived at the same shape (§1.2)
entries.axis_b: G5 The conveyor owns its whole model and is self-contained

value.objective: O1 One model, one store — the catalogue, release, binding and decision rows are conveyor rows; the agent platform is a front end and no manifest is imported (D33, D44).

entries.axis_a: D6 The programme's record is public — the design pack and the published outputs
entries.axis_b: G6 The model is published and falsifiable

value.objective: O6 The public can see and challenge the design — no certification claim outruns the rows; the artefacts and gates the organisation uses are the ones it publishes (§8.6, §13).

entries.axis_a: D2 The field builds agent conversations; organisations run on positions, work products, gates, baselines and evidence (§1.3)

value.objective: O2 TOGAF, SAFe, PMP and MSP artefacts are rows, gates and evidence, and every decision row names its option, confidence and policy (D32, D30).

entries.axis_b: G3 Every tool a job may call is versioned, bound and ledgered

value.objective: O3 Tool and toolkit versions, one effect ceiling per binding and one `tool_call` row per call; the broker is the only call path (D41, D45).

entries.axis_a: D4 The v4 lesson: the right roles on the wrong substrate (§1.4)
entries.axis_b: G4 The system builds and operates itself

entries.axis_a: D5 Three independently built things arrived at the same shape (§1.2)
entries.axis_b: G5 The conveyor owns its whole model and is self-contained

value.objective: O7 A meeting is a card whose agenda items resolve existing approvals, with typed positions, quorum, a decision rule and minutes as a governed asset (D66, §6.8).

entries.axis_a: One product must serve many tenants without a per-tenant fork (SPEC §5.1, CONTRACT §9)
entries.axis_b: Two tenants are isolated, including under RLS

value.measure: as conveyor_runtime scoped to A, count(*) FROM event returns 0 of B's rows; a forged tenant_id = B insert fails WITH CHECK; the owner also sees 0; the superuser sees both

entries.axis_a: The tenant comes from membership, never a client header (CONTRACT §9)

value.measure: Bearer dev:alice returns 200 at /api/me; with APP_ENV=production the process exits non-zero

entries.axis_a: A worker killed mid-handler must not lose or double-run durable work
entries.axis_b: A fenced lease, not a process lock, owns a job

value.measure: JOB_LEASE_SECS=2; kill -9 mid-handler; restart reclaims the row on lease expiry, attempts increments, and the stale token writes nothing

entries.axis_a: A UI must reconnect without losing or duplicating events
entries.axis_b: SSE replays by event.seq inside the subscriber's tenant scope

value.measure: three events; reconnect with Last-Event-ID of e1 returns e2 then e3 once each in seq order; B's events are absent

entries.axis_a: Audit is a record, not editable state

value.measure: UPDATE audit_event as conveyor_runtime is denied; details are capped at 8192 bytes

entries.axis_a: Entitlement fails closed and core requests never call the licences service

value.measure: no row, a row older than 3600 s, an expired, revoked or unknown status all refuse; a JWT-shaped token that fails verification is a hard 401

entries.axis_a: Migrations must be reproducible, forward-only and found from the crate that embeds them
entries.axis_b: One embedded migration set at the workspace root

value.measure: sqlx::migrate!("../../migrations") and a unit test asserting the embedded set is exactly [(1, "platform")]

entries.axis_a: D1 Fourteen aggregates with no single owning schema
entries.axis_b: G1 One baseline migration owns the tables

value.objective: migrations/0002_domain.sql creates exactly 14 tables (programme, project, board, list, card_type, card, run, approval, approval_decision, governed_asset, trace_link, catalogue_entry, revision, andon_state); `grep -c 'CREATE TABLE'` returns 14; later slices add tables but never re-invent one (S3 mandate; plan §1).

entries.axis_a: D2 A card carries its own status column, which drifts from its list
entries.axis_b: G2 list.kind is the only state

value.objective: `card` has no state or status column; `information_schema.columns` for card and (state,status) returns zero rows; `may_move` reads project_type.meta.matrix and an absent entry, card type or row denies (S3-D1, S3-D3; plan trap 1).

entries.axis_a: D3 Two claims can grant the same card
entries.axis_b: G3 A conditional claim UPDATE with a fence

value.objective: claim_card_tx is one `UPDATE … WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND id = $2 AND version = $5 AND (lease_expires_at IS NULL OR lease_expires_at < now() OR assignee_id = $3) RETURNING claim_fence, version`; claim_fence rises on every grant and release is fenced. The lease arm also lets the current assignee renew, so the exclusive reading is the P1 package v1-s03-1.

entries.axis_a: D4 Two pending approvals per (run, gate)
entries.axis_b: G4 A partial unique index is the guarantee

value.objective: uq_appr_pending (tenant_id, run_id, gate) WHERE status='pending'; a duplicate is 23505 and maps to ApprovalConflict; sixteen concurrent inserts yield one pending row. A NULL run_id escapes the index; the card-level path is S06's (plan trap 5).

entries.axis_a: D5 ENABLE RLS still lets the table owner read everything
entries.axis_b: G5 FORCE RLS on all fourteen tables

value.objective: every table carries tenant_id, ENABLE and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and the tenant_isolation policy; as conveyor_runtime scoped to A, B's rows are absent and a forged tenant_id=B insert fails WITH CHECK; the owner sees 0 and a superuser both (plan trap 7).

entries.axis_a: D6 Porting fr's 224-migration accretion is the largest failure mode
entries.axis_b: G6 The baseline is SPEC §6, not fr's history

value.objective: R10: a column enters only because §2.3/§2.4 names it; a deviation is a contract change; the schema-review step checks every table line by line and records a reviewed list rather than a silent drift (plan trap 10).

entries.axis_a: D7 Archive has two notions — a lane and a stamp — that can disagree

value.objective: archived_at IS NOT NULL implies list.kind='archive', proved by board.rs::archived_implies_the_card_sits_in_an_archive_list; restore off a non-archive list is an error. The stronger claim that every hot index filters archived cards is true only of the two board-scan indexes — the P2 package v1-s03-2.

entries.axis_b: G1 One baseline migration owns the tables

value.objective: migrations/0002_domain.sql creates exactly 14 tables (programme, project, board, list, card_type, card, run, approval, approval_decision, governed_asset, trace_link, catalogue_entry, revision, andon_state); `grep -c 'CREATE TABLE'` returns 14; later slices add tables but never re-invent one (S3 mandate; plan §1).

entries.axis_a: D2 A card carries its own status column, which drifts from its list
entries.axis_b: G2 list.kind is the only state

value.objective: `card` has no state or status column; `information_schema.columns` for card and (state,status) returns zero rows; `may_move` reads project_type.meta.matrix and an absent entry, card type or row denies (S3-D1, S3-D3; plan trap 1).

entries.axis_a: D3 Two claims can grant the same card
entries.axis_b: G3 A conditional claim UPDATE with a fence

value.objective: claim_card_tx is one `UPDATE … WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND id = $2 AND version = $5 AND (lease_expires_at IS NULL OR lease_expires_at < now() OR assignee_id = $3) RETURNING claim_fence, version`; claim_fence rises on every grant and release is fenced. The lease arm also lets the current assignee renew, so the exclusive reading is the P1 package v1-s03-1.

entries.axis_a: D4 Two pending approvals per (run, gate)
entries.axis_b: G4 A partial unique index is the guarantee

value.objective: uq_appr_pending (tenant_id, run_id, gate) WHERE status='pending'; a duplicate is 23505 and maps to ApprovalConflict; sixteen concurrent inserts yield one pending row. A NULL run_id escapes the index; the card-level path is S06's (plan trap 5).

entries.axis_a: D5 ENABLE RLS still lets the table owner read everything
entries.axis_b: G5 FORCE RLS on all fourteen tables

value.objective: every table carries tenant_id, ENABLE and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and the tenant_isolation policy; as conveyor_runtime scoped to A, B's rows are absent and a forged tenant_id=B insert fails WITH CHECK; the owner sees 0 and a superuser both (plan trap 7).

entries.axis_a: D6 Porting fr's 224-migration accretion is the largest failure mode
entries.axis_b: G6 The baseline is SPEC §6, not fr's history

value.objective: R10: a column enters only because §2.3/§2.4 names it; a deviation is a contract change; the schema-review step checks every table line by line and records a reviewed list rather than a silent drift (plan trap 10).

entries.axis_a: D7 Archive has two notions — a lane and a stamp — that can disagree

value.objective: archived_at IS NOT NULL implies list.kind='archive', proved by board.rs::archived_implies_the_card_sits_in_an_archive_list; restore off a non-archive list is an error. The stronger claim that every hot index filters archived cards is true only of the two board-scan indexes — the P2 package v1-s03-2.

artifacts.purpose: The drivers behind the baseline domain, the goal each serves and the objective the migration and the machines install.
artifacts.scope: one migration, list-as-state, claim and lease, approval uniqueness, FORCE RLS, the anti-accretion rule and the archive invariant.
artifacts.title: Driver/Goal/Objective Catalog — S03 Domain and schema (Phase A)

entries.axis_a: D1 280 board↔project lookup flows duplicated across board surfaces
entries.axis_b: G1 One foreign-key read: project_type.meta.matrix through may_move

value.objective: cards.move loads the card, both lists and project.project_type_code, then reads `SELECT e.meta->'matrix'->$card_type_code->>$from_kind FROM catalogue_entry e WHERE e.tenant_id=$1 AND e.kind='project_type' AND e.code=$project_type_code AND e.is_active`; an absent row, type, from-kind or a kind not in the array is 409 card-move-not-allowed; the lookup is cached per (tenant, project_type_code) (plan §5; the S03 matrix).

entries.axis_a: D2 Multiple comment and membership stores across Planka and fr
entries.axis_b: G2 One comment table and one board_membership row

value.objective: comment is the only thread store; board_membership carries role owner|admin|member|viewer with can_comment and watching; project_manager and board_subscription fold into that row; editor maps to member; a card's assignee is card.assignee_id; no card_membership and no attachment table (plan §5; gate property f).

entries.axis_b: G3 The group is carried in two columns, never joined

value.objective: custom_field.group_name and group_position replace the group entity; the field is board data, not vocabulary — no catalogue_entry row; kind is text|number|date|select|checkbox validated in the domain; values upsert on (card_id, custom_field_id) (plan §5, S5-D3).

entries.axis_a: D4 A synchronous webhook POST couples a mutation to a third party
entries.axis_b: G4 Emit from the event row through a job

value.objective: one job(kind='webhook.deliver', dedupe_key=<event>:<subscription>) per matching subscription, drained with an Authorization Bearer secret, 15 s timeout, 3 attempts; events[] and excluded_events[] select subscriptions (plan §5, S5-D7).

entries.axis_a: D5 A second write path would bypass audit, idempotency and webhooks
entries.axis_b: G5 Every write is an action

value.objective: zero REST write routes; the 39 actions are POST /api/actions/{name}/invocations; every mutation writes its event row in the same transaction (plan §3, S5-D2).

entries.axis_a: D6 Floating-point positions drift after repeated midpoint inserts
entries.axis_b: G6 numeric midpoints, append max+1024, board advisory lock

value.objective: (a+b)/2 between neighbours and max+1024 on append, never float; reads use cursors, never OFFSET, because concurrent drags skip and duplicate rows (plan §8 traps 2 and 6).

entries.axis_a: D7 Event-name drift between the internal register and Planka camelCase
entries.axis_b: G7 Internal register names owned by S05

value.objective: card.moved and card.archived, not cards.moved; the emitter body is {event,data,prevData,user} with the *Out field names (list_id, not listId); Planka's cardCreate/cardUpdate vocabulary is a deferred S14 cutover adapter, never a second emitter (plan §5, gate property d).

entries.axis_a: D8 The live Planka database holds five test cards and cannot be gate evidence
entries.axis_b: G8 A defined key-referenced export and generated fixtures

value.objective: board-export/v1 references keys, not UUIDs; two committed fixtures (v1-recording.json: 1 board, 5 lists, 20 cards, 30 comments, 40 tasks, 6 fields, seed 7; v1-1000.json: 1,000 cards, 10 lists, seed 42); four subcommands fixture|import|export|diff; archives are excluded (plan §5, S5-D1).

artifacts.title: Driver/Goal/Objective Catalog — S05 Board (Phase A)

entries.axis_a: D1 Competing claim paths leave a card race without one decision boundary
entries.axis_b: G1 One conditional UPDATE per claim, with a monotonic claim_fence as the ABA witness

value.objective: cards.claim runs one statement: `UPDATE card SET assignee_id=$3, lease_expires_at=now()+$4::interval, lease_token=uuidv7(), claim_fence=claim_fence+1, version=version+1 ... WHERE tenant_id=$1 AND id=$2 AND version=$5 AND (lease_expires_at IS NULL OR lease_expires_at < now() OR assignee_id=$3) RETURNING claim_fence, version`. $5 is the caller's `If-Match`, a mismatch is 412, zero rows is a refusal, and a blocked claimant enqueues one deduped `card.claim` job (plan §5, decision 1).

entries.axis_a: D2 fr runs 14 timers and three duplicate rollups outside one durable runner
entries.axis_b: G2 Every cadence is a schedule row and an idempotent job on (kind, dedupe_key)

value.objective: the 11 surviving fr timers become job kinds (schedule.materialise, approval.closed.emit, approval.expire, approval.redeliver, deblock.redeliver, coverage.redeliver, project.reconcile, schedule.health, idempotency.sweep, job.prune and the S07-deferred project_request.timeout), each deduped by key; analytics-rollup, signup-onboarding-tick and workflows-cache are deleted; periods are schedule rows under one advisory lock (plan §5.3, decision 9).

entries.axis_a: D3 Approvals were split across web, Telegram and mcp with no shared decision path
entries.axis_b: G3 One approvals.decide action with required_decisions and decided_by_kind

value.objective: at most one pending approval per (run, gate) by partial unique index; dual control is `required_decisions`, a person cannot decide twice by unique constraint, a close is pending → approved iff count(approve) >= required_decisions or pending → rejected on any reject in one transaction, and `decided_by_kind` records human or agent (plan §5.4).

entries.axis_a: D4 An andon cord tied to a live process could not survive a restart
entries.axis_b: G4 Andon is an andon_state row, a 409 refusal and a worker-scraped gauge

value.objective: andon.engage writes andon_state and emits andon.engaged; runs.create refuses 409 andon-engaged; the poller skips engaged tenants; release reverses both; the worker exposes conveyor_andon_engaged and conveyor_andon_engaged_at_seconds with a 1 s timeout so a dead exporter alarms via absent() (plan §5.5, decision 6).

entries.axis_a: D5 Notification fan-out lacked per-recipient delivery semantics and retry
entries.axis_b: G5 One message plus N delivery rows, sent outside the transaction with bounded backoff

value.objective: messages.send writes one message and N delivery rows, each enqueueing delivery.send on dedupe_key=delivery.id; the drainer claims with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED plus lease_token, sends outside the transaction, moves pending → sent → delivered | failed | expired, and backs off min(2^attempts · 5 s, 900 s) (plan §5.6).

entries.axis_a: D6 Control-plane consumers needed live topics and replay without polling
entries.axis_b: G6 Three SSE topics fed by the in-transaction event row and pg_notify

value.objective: run:{id}, approval:{id} and tenant are the control-plane topics; every mutation writes its event row in the same transaction and pg_notify carries it; a second client replays with Last-Event-ID and the 17 event types are owned by S06 (plan §5.6).

entries.axis_a: D7 A decision needed to record whether a human or an agent made it
entries.axis_b: G7 decided_by_kind plus via records the actor class and the surface

value.objective: approvals.decide records decided_by_kind human (web or Telegram) or agent (/mcp, D19) and via (channel, agent_member_id, product); property (g) drives one decision of each kind through the same action, so S06a depends on S06 and never the reverse (plan §5.4, §7 property g).

entries.axis_a: D8 An inbound Telegram reply had no settled sender identity (#4)
entries.axis_b: G8 Resolve (chat_id, topic_id) → channel_binding → tenant → sender and call the shared actions

value.objective: the Telegram inbound route POST /api/channels/telegram/{binding_id} authenticates by secret-token header, resolves the binding and tenant to a sender, and calls the same approvals.decide or cards.comment the web does, with no per-channel decision path; issue #4 records that the shared decision boundary and the sender identity were still open at the snapshot.

entries.axis_b: G1 One governed_asset lifecycle for requirements, principles and decisions

entries.axis_a: D1 Bytes stored in Postgres TOAST every row and every dump
entries.axis_b: G1 Bytes live in MinIO behind one authorized stream

value.objective: object_store writes bucket conveyor-documents at key t/<tenant>/<document>/<version>; every byte streams through /api/documents/{id}/content authenticated against tenant_id and membership; no presigned URL exists (plan 5.2, decision 1).

entries.axis_a: D2 A secret returned once for convenience is the whole leak
entries.axis_b: G2 Secrets are write-only and never revealed

value.objective: create and rotate take value marked x-secret; get and list return id, name, scope, key_id, version and created_at only; there is no reveal action and OpenAPI examples are stripped for marked fields (plan 5.4, traps 2 and 3).

entries.axis_a: D3 One direct read of a neighbour's database owns its schema and its outages
entries.axis_b: G3 Every adjacent service is a declared action

value.objective: a call absent from action_registry does not exist; action_registry.service names the backing service; reads carry a 5 s timeout and writes 30 s; the breaker is process-local and opens after five failures in 30 s (plan 5.1, decision 7).

entries.axis_a: D4 Ingestion could become a second local pipeline
entries.axis_b: G4 documents.ingest is an internal action over the strata service

value.objective: documents.ingest is registered once as kind internal and pushes multipart to strata_ingest POST /api/ingest/jobs with the tenant token sealed as strata_ingest.token; the returned jobs[0].job_id is stored in document.external_ref (plan 5.6, decision 10).

entries.axis_a: D5 Cloning repositories would make the conveyor a git host

value.objective: repository holds provider, url, default_branch, installation_ref and credential_secret_id; project_repository is the join with role; coding work is coding_jobs.create with repository_url and ref returning run.external_ref; no git crate may appear in the dependency tree (plan 5.3, decision 6).

entries.axis_a: D6 Rolled-up metrics drift from the operational tables
entries.axis_b: G6 Every report number is a live query

value.objective: reports are document rows of kind report carrying meta.params and meta.generated_at; each number is computed on demand from event, card, list, run, approval, approval_decision and delivery; project_metrics stays dropped (plan 5.5, decision 8).

entries.axis_a: D7 Worker scheduling and billing logic are other systems' authority
entries.axis_b: G7 Workers, billing and observability are read-only displays

value.objective: the workers page renders the external answer with no writes and no local table; billing.summary reads inference_call and tool_call and billing display adds app_licence as of checked_at with no arithmetic, metering write or budget mutation (plan 5.5, decision 9).

entries.axis_a: D8 A marked secret leaking into a published OpenAPI example
entries.axis_b: G8 The served spec strips marked examples and asserts

value.objective: utoipa and the MCP projection carry x-secret on the value field and publish no default or example for it; the served-spec lock is regenerated only through the binary's --print-openapi --write-lock and checked by --check-lock (build step 8, trap 3).

entries.axis_a: D9 A delete that drops the row and leaves the object
entries.axis_b: G9 Tombstone first, purge guarded by status

value.objective: documents.delete sets status deleted and enqueues document.purge; the purge checks status == deleted before removing bytes and clear_object_tx refuses a non-deleted row, so orphaned bytes and pointerless documents are both refused (plan 5.2, trap 0b).

entries.axis_a: D1 Estate services are called ad hoc, outside the governed tool path
entries.axis_b: G1 Every estate tool is a toolkit called through the broker

value.objective: each live service is imported as tool, toolkit and tool_binding rows and invoked through tools.call, so every call leaves one tool_call row; a direct backend call is not part of T14 (T13's broker, SPEC_V2 §11).

entries.axis_a: D2 A toolkit could be published without proof that it works
entries.axis_b: G2 A probe and one live call precede publication

value.objective: each published toolkit carries a probe receipt and one live-call receipt; publication is the act the gate guards, and a draft is never counted as published (SPEC_V2 §12 T14 gate).

entries.axis_a: D3 scientific_processor is scarce host compute and must not be left scaled up
entries.axis_b: G3 Scale up for the probe and live call, then scale back with a receipt

value.objective: the slice records a scale-up before the probe and the live call and a scale-back afterwards; an unrecorded scale or a left-up host is a gate failure, not an optimisation (SPEC_V2 §12 T14 gate).

entries.axis_a: D4 Unused toolkits accumulate cost and risk with no retirement pressure
entries.axis_b: G4 A zero-use report feeds the provenance and retirement gate

value.objective: a zero-use report exists over tool_call activity and feeds the executable tool-provenance and retirement gate named by issue 558, so an unused toolkit has a recorded exit path.

entries.axis_a: D5 A backend outage can stall or corrupt new runs
entries.axis_b: G5 An outage unbinds new runs and in-flight runs finish

value.objective: the outage-unbind test kills a backend and asserts that new runs are refused at binding while in-flight runs complete; the behaviour is proved by the test, never asserted from the design.

entries.axis_a: D6 Unfinished services would be indistinguishable from published ones
entries.axis_b: G6 Draft is an explicit state

value.objective: evidence_review, discovery :8807 and the planned AHTAPol services enter as draft; the draft state is visible in the record and cannot satisfy the published-toolkit gate clause.

entries.axis_a: D7 A second tool registry would fork governance
entries.axis_b: G7 One import wave onto T13's family

value.objective: T14 adds rows and receipts to the T13 tool, toolkit, tool_binding and tool_call family; it creates no second registry, no second broker and no second credential store.

entries.axis_a: D8 Gate claims have been made without receipts
entries.axis_b: G8 A claim without a receipt is recorded as open verification

value.objective: meta.measured_status says built, but the snapshot carries no probe, live-call, scale, zero-use or unbind receipt; the rework records that gap as the project's open verification item instead of inferring a pass from the word built.

value.objective: project_baseline stores an immutable approved snapshot of the WBS, register and budget facts; a later row edit never moves it (D-T1-2; plan_spine.rs::a_baseline_does_not_move_when_rows_change).

entries.axis_a: D2 A change can happen by a silent row edit
entries.axis_b: G2 Change control with an impact block

value.objective: a change is project_register_item(kind='change') carrying a required impact block and a baseline_ref; without them the row is refused 422 change_impact_missing (D-T1-3; P1.2).

entries.axis_a: D3 A requester can decide the gate judging their work
entries.axis_b: G3 Dual control on every gate

value.objective: approvals.decide compares the pending row's requested_by (and the executor) with the actor and refuses before an approval_decision row is written, for every gate (D-T1-8; approval_dual.rs::the_requester_cannot_decide_their_own_gate).

entries.axis_a: D4 Priority is opinion, and a stored score goes stale

value.objective: WSJF = (business_value + time_criticality + risk_reduction) / job_size, computed on read from four non-negative integers with job_size > 0; no score column exists (D-T1-4; P2.1).

entries.axis_a: D5 No one can say what is in flight

value.objective: portfolio.in_flight is a read model with no row over the tenant's configured status set, default active,paused (D-T1-7; P3.1).

entries.axis_a: D6 Dependency order is a JSON list that cannot express edges or cycles

value.objective: project_dependency edges are blocks|needs|supersedes|informs; a cycle is refused 409 dependency_cycle by a recursive reachability query in the creating transaction, leaving no partial row (D-T1-5/D-T1-6; P4.1, P4.2).

entries.axis_a: D7 A benefit is prose and a review can be evidence-free
entries.axis_b: G7 A benefit is a measurement record and a tranche review carries evidence

value.objective: benefit_profile requires baseline, target, measurement_method and a benefit owner; benefit_link names all five levels; tranches.review requires baselines, benefit status and the risk register (D-T1-9/D-T1-10; P5.1–P5.3).

entries.axis_a: D1 Three decision rungs read as three different records
entries.axis_b: G1 One audit shape across L0, L1 and L3

value.objective: `decision` carries rung, answer, option-set version, policy/refinement/laya-config pins, actor, outcome and approval link for every rung; `decision_ladder.rs::a_rule_a_laya_and_a_human_decision_share_one_audit_shape` asserts the three rows have identical column sets.

entries.axis_a: D2 A threshold change needs a build and a deploy
entries.axis_b: G2 A tenant refinement changes a threshold as configuration

value.objective: `decision_policy_refinement` overrides the threshold, rule and fail action for one policy; `decision_policy_refinement_one_per_policy` keeps one live row and bumps its version. `decision_ladder.rs::a_refinement_changes_a_threshold_without_a_code_change` moves 0.7 from refused to accepted at 0.5.

entries.axis_a: D3 A decision cannot be reproduced after the policy moves
entries.axis_b: G3 Every decision pins the versions it read

value.objective: the decision row records `policy_version`, `refinement_version` and `laya_config_version`; an L1 decision with no config to pin is refused `422 pins_incomplete`; `decision_ladder.rs::every_decision_pins_the_refinement_and_laya_config_versions` leaves the first row at version 1 after the policy moves to version 2.

entries.axis_a: D4 A generated draft can move a card
entries.axis_b: G4 L2 has no transition path; applying a draft is a human gate

value.objective: `ladder.apply_draft` requires an accepted human `draft.apply` decision backed by an approved `draft.apply` approval on the same card; `documents.update` refuses the generated class with `409 draft_requires_gate`. `decision_ladder.rs::a_generated_draft_cannot_transition_a_card` and `ladder_human_gate.rs::only_a_human_draft_apply_decision_can_gate_a_draft` prove the update and apply paths.

entries.axis_a: D5 The create path can still attach a generated draft

value.objective: OPEN — v1-t2-1: `documents.compose` accepts `card_id` and `meta.generated = true` and writes an attached document with no gate, so the fourth gate clause is not universally true and T2 stays active.

entries.axis_a: D6 A human decision can cite any approved approval
entries.axis_b: G6 A human decision cites the gate that posed its question

value.objective: OPEN — v1-t2-6: `ladder.record` calls `human_approved_gate_tx(..., None, card_id)`, so the `gate` field is not compared with `approval.gate`; only `ladder.apply_draft` passes `Some(DRAFT_APPLY_GATE)`. `ladder_human_gate.rs::a_human_decision_without_an_approved_human_gate_is_refused` checks approval status and human decider, not gate identity.

entries.axis_a: D7 Options and questions are free text in a prompt
entries.axis_b: G7 Options and questions are authored, versioned rows

value.objective: PARTIAL — v1-t2-4: `ladder.evaluate` accepts inline `options: [{key, label, payload}]` and a free `question` string, and `decision_policy` carries kind/gate/threshold/fail_policy/action, not an authored question with `fire_when` and `min_confidence`.

entries.axis_a: D8 L1 is recorded but never asks laya
entries.axis_b: G8 The L1 answer comes from the laya client

value.objective: OPEN — v1-t2-2: `ladder.evaluate` records the caller's `answer`, `confidence`, `probabilities` and `latency_ms`; `laya_configs` pins model_ref/params/timeout_ms but no T2 path calls `POST /v1/systemone`.

entries.axis_a: D9 The generation budget has no §7.5 refusal
entries.axis_b: G9 Refuse over budget before the next call

value.objective: OPEN — v1-t2-5: SPEC_V2 §7.5 records `429 budget_exceeded`; T2 enforces no inference budget, and the only budget refusal in the tree is the tool-spend `429 tool_budget_exceeded` (`crates/actions/src/invoke.rs`, `crates/actions/src/broker.rs`, #526).

artifacts.title: Requirements catalog — S02 Skeleton

value.statement: tenant, app_user, department, membership, event, job, schedule, audit_event, action_invocation, idempotency_key and app_licence; no others
every store function takes TenantId as its first argument after the connection; begin_scoped sets app.current_tenant with set_config($1, $2, true); no session-level SET appears

the nine tenant-owned tables are ENABLE + FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, each with one FOR ALL tenant_isolation policy carrying USING and WITH CHECK; membership adds one SELECT-only membership_self_read policy TO conveyor_runtime

conveyor_migrate is the owner; conveyor_runtime is LOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS; migrate asserts rolsuper = false and rolbypassrls = false and aborts otherwise; REVOKE ALL ON _sqlx_migrations FROM conveyor_runtime

entries.axis_b: An unlisted issuer is never fetched

value.statement: one realm conveyor; an unlisted iss is rejected before any JWKS fetch; per-issuer cache TTL 600 s with a 30 s negative floor; aud and azp are both required

CONVEYOR_DEV_AUTH=1 accepts Bearer dev:<login> or the conveyor_dev=<login> cookie; membership must resolve exactly one (app_user, tenant) or the request is a 401; migrate --dev-seed creates dev-a/alice and dev-b/bob; startup exits non-zero if set with APP_ENV=production

RequireLicence reads app_licence only; absent, stale beyond 3600 s, expired, revoked or unknown refuses; a JWT-shaped token that fails verification is a hard 401, never retried as a licence token; licence.sync refreshes the row

claim is FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED with lease_token and lease_until; an expired lease is reclaimed and attempts increments; finish/retry are guarded by status = 'running' AND lease_token = $token; schedules materialise under pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('conveyor:schedule'))
audit_event grants SELECT and INSERT only; UPDATE and DELETE are revoked after the schema-wide GRANT; action matches ^[a-z0-9_]+\.[a-z0-9_]+$; details are capped at 8192 bytes

Last-Event-ID is event.seq; replay is seq > $last AND topic = ANY($topics) ORDER BY seq LIMIT 500 in the subscriber's tenant scope; 15 s keepalive; a 64-slot channel closes a slow client with resync; the LISTEN connection is direct because PgBouncer is transaction-pooled
GET /health, /health/live, /health/ready, /metrics, /api/me and /api/events; /api is one OpenApiRouter built with .routes(); --print-openapi emits the document and exits before config/DB
db on 5439 (postgres -p 5439), pgbouncer on 6439, app on 8930; integration tests start their own ephemeral container on a random host port; a container that cannot start fails, never skips

entries.axis_b: trace_links.* is the only writer of trace_link

value.acceptance: a requirement-to-card link reads back from both the requirement with include=trace and the card's traces endpoint, in the same tenant, with zero cross-tenant rows.

entries.axis_b: Project requests are idempotent and promote atomically

value.acceptance: project_requests are unique on (tenant, external_ref), move through draft, approved, rejected and promoted, and promote creates its project through the store in the same transaction rather than re-calling projects.create.

entries.axis_b: Every mutation writes one outbox event in its transaction

value.acceptance: eleven event types cover governed_asset.created/updated/transitioned/superseded, quality.evaluated, catalogue.imported and the four project_request transitions plus promoted, with the payload keys fixed in plan §5.8.

value.acceptance: the six API and store test targets, the ignored search_eval run and the EXPLAIN block that greps governed_asset_tsv_idx or governed_asset_title_trgm_idx; search_index asserts the index by name as conveyor_runtime.

artifacts.change_initiative: The SPEC V2 operating-model adoption (tranche 0, retrospective rework #526)

value.acceptance: No concept is stored in two systems; systems join by pinned reference (P1, §10.1).
No work without a card; no transition without an action; no completion without evidence (P3).

entries.axis_b: The executor never approves its own work

value.acceptance: Dual control on gates; `decided_by_kind`; the approver is neither the assignee nor the executor (P4).
An unresolved binding, pack, prompt source or tool refuses `409 *_not_ready` with `blocking[]` before the first model call or action (P8).

entries.axis_b: Every model call is ledgered and budgeted

value.acceptance: `inference_call` rows with per-run and per-tenant budgets (P9).
A table exists because a named procedure uses it and a metric reads it; an unused aggregate is removed, not defended (P10, D40).
Every policy, threshold, limit, gate condition and approval kind is a versioned tenant-scoped row with a platform default; code implements mechanisms, never policy values (P11, D50).

entries.axis_b: Immutable releases; a stale binding refuses

value.acceptance: A binding pins `job_key` + `release_hash` + an immutable `release_snapshot`; a run against a retired binding refuses `409 job_binding_stale` before any model call (D38).
Every tool declares one of read | write | destructive | spend; a binding's ceiling narrows only; destructive needs a dry-run and the tenant's configured approvals (D45, §11.4).
A benefit without baseline, target, method and owner is refused; the benefits map names output → capability → operational outcome → benefit → objective (D62, §8.3).

entries.axis_b: A delivery project needs its governing contract

value.acceptance: A delivery project cannot pass design without the live contract that governs it; a Phase-G review records exactly one of the six standard levels (D63, §8.1).

entries.axis_b: The agent platform is a front end

value.acceptance: It is a conversation surface over MCP with its own autonomy configuration — not a catalogue, an executor or a system of record for conveyor work (D33, D59).

entries.axis_b: laya answers inside the seam budget

value.acceptance: `POST /v1/systemone`, 1500 ms default / 3 s hard budget, fail policy per decision policy; a timeout never becomes an LLM decision (§10.2, §7).
V1 D1–D27 stand except D14 and D22, which V2 amends (D46, D61); no V1 S-slice is re-opened.

entries.axis_b: Procedural knowledge has no ontology store

value.acceptance: Amended 2026-11-19: RDF/OWL/Turtle is imported as a strata knowledge pack named by the procedure's `knowledge_pack_ref`; the conveyor runs no RDF store, no graph store and no reasoner (D53, §5.6).

A run naming a retired binding, or a release other than the binding's pin, is 409 job_binding_stale naming both hashes before any model call. crates/store/tests/organisation.rs::a_run_pins_its_binding_and_a_retired_or_mismatched_pin_is_refused; the action surface in crates/actions/tests/sop_ingestion.rs::a_bound_job_runs_the_pddl_steps.

The SPEC_V2 §10.1 ownership matrix assigns each fact one system of record; job_catalogue, job_release and job_binding join the conveyor's own rows; there is no imported manifest and no live copy of another system's data.

executor_kind is an open slug (^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,31}$) stored as TEXT with no value CHECK; a test-only third kind registers and resolves without editing the run path. crates/domain/src/executor.rs; crates/store/tests/organisation.rs::third_executor_kind_registers_without_editing_the_run_path.
The five decision tables exist with FORCE RLS and no evaluation path is added (T2). migrations/0040_organisation.sql; crates/actions/tests/decision_ladder.rs exercises the audit shape T2 will use.

Every organisation action is one ActionSpec served over HTTP, MCP and OpenAPI and pinned in served-spec.lock.json: industries.create|get|list, departments.create|list, job_catalogue.create|update|retire|get|list, job_releases.publish|retire|list, job_bindings.create|retire|get|list.

Every tenant-owned table carries tenant_id, ENABLE and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and the tenant_isolation policy; the seed proves AHTAPol sees only its industry. crates/store/tests/organisation.rs::ahtapol_receives_only_its_industry.

value.acceptance: The five read actions return aggregates over ledger rows and write no metric row. crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::a_level_moves_only_when_the_evidence_crosses_the_recorded_threshold counts four threshold rows and zero reconciliation rows after the reads; migrations/0059_metrics.sql creates no metric table.

entries.axis_b: Every metering level sums to its children

value.acceptance: crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::every_metering_level_sums_to_its_children: tenant 3 calls and 3,150 tokens; project, programme, run, department, job and call each return the same 3 calls and 3,150 tokens; an unattributed caller-kind `other` call appears in its own bucket; a new ledger row changes the figure on the next read.

entries.axis_b: The run drill-down sums to its call rows

value.acceptance: crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::the_run_drilldown_sums_to_the_call_rows: the run's steps and its calls each sum to 4,500 tokens, and the per-step cost sums to the run cost within 1e-9.

entries.axis_b: Flow recomputes; a missing ledger is unavailable, not zero

value.acceptance: crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::flow_recomputes_and_a_missing_ledger_is_unavailable: throughput 1, lead 3,600 s, cycle 1,800 s, queue 1,800 s, block 540 s and flow efficiency 0.35, each within its stated tolerance; knowledge.lesson_promotion_rate is listed in `unavailable` with the reason that the T8 ledger does not exist.

crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::a_level_moves_only_when_the_evidence_crosses_the_recorded_threshold: C1 versions 1, 2 and 3 are three append-only rows and no code changes; each read names the version that authorised the level.

entries.axis_b: A level moves only when evidence crosses its recorded threshold, with no gaps

value.acceptance: The same test: five approvals at rate 1.0 meet C1 v1; one rejection lowers the rate to 0.833 and still meets 0.8; raising the recorded threshold to 0.9 drops the level back to C0 without changing the evidence; lowering it to 0.8 returns C1 at v3. crates/domain/src/metrics.rs::a_missing_metric_never_lifts_a_level and current_level stop at the first unmet level.

entries.axis_b: Reconciliation is exact to six decimals or opens an incident

value.acceptance: crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::reconciliation_is_exact_or_opens_an_incident: total 0.002 matches with delta 0; total 0.003 is `difference` and opens an `incident` card whose meta records conveyor_usd 0.002 and billing_usd 0.003; a 503 is `unavailable` with the upstream error and null figures, never zero. crates/domain/src/metrics.rs::reconciliation_is_exact_to_six_decimals fixes the precision.

entries.axis_b: A gate that never refused is flagged

value.acceptance: crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::a_gate_with_no_refusal_is_flagged_and_one_refusal_clears_it: tranche_review with 3 approvals and 0 rejections is in `never_refused`; one rejection removes it; benefit_review's pending approvals are untouched; latency is reported.

entries.axis_b: Cost is derived from the pinned price catalogue, never stored

value.acceptance: crates/store/src/metrics.rs joins commercial_price on model and unit at read time and returns cost_usd plus priced_calls and unpriced_calls; migrations/0059_metrics.sql states that no metric is stored; the snapshot's measure note fixes cost as a read-time derivation.

migrations/0059_metrics.sql enables and forces RLS with the tenant_isolation policy on metric_threshold and metric_reconciliation; crates/store/tests/rls_domain.rs::metric_thresholds_are_tenant_isolated proves tenant A sees only its C0 row and a forged write under A's scope for tenant B fails WITH CHECK.

entries.axis_b: The eight metrics actions are one served contract surface

value.acceptance: served-spec.lock.json pins metrics.flow, metrics.job, metrics.usage, metrics.programme, metrics.maturity, metrics.reconcile, metrics.threshold_get and metrics.threshold_update; each is an ActionSpec projected to HTTP and MCP; docs/evidence/v2-coverage.json records actions:metrics at 8/8, modules 3/3 and tables 2/2.

entries.axis_b: The console Metering screen reads live aggregates and never borrows a fixture

value.acceptance: docs/design/v2.js meteringLive() renders measure.inference totals, by caller and by model from the published snapshot; docs/design/scripts/check-v2.cjs 9b–9d assert the live rows, no fixture figure, the snapshot's cost note and the no-measure sentence (#458).

value.acceptance: a_bound_job_calls_coding_through_the_broker: 200, one destination hit, /api/jobs reached
value.requirement: tools.call resolves the binding and dispatches to the registered coding destination alias

entries.axis_b: one call writes exactly one ledger row and one event

value.acceptance: one_call_is_one_ledger_row: one row for the call, one tool.called event
value.requirement: tool_call carries run, step, tool version, input hash, status, latency, bytes and cost, and is not action_invocation

entries.axis_b: a destructive call without the tenant's configured approvals is refused

value.acceptance: a_destructive_call_without_approvals_is_refused: 403 approval_required, zero hits, no row
value.requirement: effect class destructive requires approval, dry-run and dual control before dispatch

entries.axis_b: schema-invalid input is refused before the backend call

value.acceptance: a_closed_schema_refuses_before_the_call: zero hits for three invalid documents, one hit for the valid one
value.requirement: a closed JSON-Schema subset with additionalProperties false, enums, patterns and bounds, returning 422 tool_input_invalid with errors[]

entries.axis_b: a job writes and reads a tenant-prefixed object with no S3 key in the prompt

value.acceptance: a_job_round_trips_a_tenant_prefixed_object: prefix, hash, read-back, wrong-hash refusal, head and traversal refusal
value.requirement: the storage adapter builds every key under tenant/<tenant_id>/ with project and run prefixes, a sha256 content hash and a size cap

entries.axis_b: the compiled prompt carries no credential or S3 key

value.acceptance: the_compiled_prompt_carries_no_s3_key
value.requirement: copilot_system@1 compiles without the access-key, secret-key or CONVEYOR_S3_ sentinels

entries.axis_b: the binding row, not a compiled constant, decides access

value.acceptance: extra tests: missing credential 409 tool_not_ready; a call-time ceiling raise is refused
value.requirement: a missing binding or missing credential is 409 tool_not_ready; a binding narrows the grant and cannot raise it at call time

entries.axis_b: the broker injects the binding's sealed credential by alias

value.acceptance: a_call_uses_the_bindings_sealed_credential sends the binding's token, not the tenant default
value.requirement: the credential is resolved from the sealed secret table and injected only at the destination, never carried by the prompt or the ledger

entries.axis_b: a keyed write replays rather than duplicates

value.acceptance: a_required_key_is_forwarded_and_replays: one destination call for two keyed calls
value.requirement: writes take an idempotency_key, replay the stored response and never make a second destination call

entries.axis_b: every refusal is asserted on the wire, not on an error string

value.acceptance: the stub hit count is asserted at zero for each refusal path
value.requirement: the proving suite uses a counting HTTP stub, so a refusal that called upstream moves the counter and fails

entries.axis_a: R1 Probe and live call per published toolkit

value.acceptance: the record shows scientific_processor scaled up for the probe and the live call and scaled back afterwards; a missing scale-back or an unrecorded scale fails the clause.

entries.axis_b: A rule, a laya and a human decision share one audit shape

value.acceptance: `decision_ladder.rs::a_rule_a_laya_and_a_human_decision_share_one_audit_shape` lists three rows with identical column sets and distinct rungs rule, laya and human; every row names `policy_id`, `policy_version`, `answer`, `confidence`, `actor_kind` and `latency_ms`.

entries.axis_b: A tenant refinement changes a threshold with no code change

value.acceptance: `decision_ladder.rs::a_refinement_changes_a_threshold_without_a_code_change` publishes a 0.5 override on a 0.8 policy and the same 0.7 answer moves from `refused` to `accepted`, pinning refinement version 1 and policy version 1.

entries.axis_b: Every decision pins the policy, refinement and laya-config versions it read

value.acceptance: `decision_ladder.rs::every_decision_pins_the_refinement_and_laya_config_versions`: an L1 decision with no laya config is `422 pins_incomplete`; with one, the row pins policy 1, refinement 1 and laya config 1; after the policy moves to 2, the stored first row still reads 1.

entries.axis_b: A generated draft cannot transition a card on the apply or update path

value.acceptance: `decision_ladder.rs::a_generated_draft_cannot_transition_a_card` refuses a refused L1 decision and an accepted L1 decision with 422 `draft_requires_gate`; the human `draft.apply` decision backed by an approved gate on the card applies the draft; `documents.update` attaching the generated class is 409 `draft_requires_gate`; `ladder_human_gate.rs::only_a_human_draft_apply_decision_can_gate_a_draft` bars a routine accepted decision.

entries.axis_b: A generated draft cannot be attached by `documents.compose`

value.acceptance: OPEN — v1-t2-1: `documents.compose` accepts `card_id` and `meta.generated = true` and creates an attached document with no `draft.apply` check. This is the P0 finding that blocks the fourth clause and the project's closure.

entries.axis_b: A human decision is a person's act on a resolved human approval

value.acceptance: `ladder_human_gate.rs::a_service_principal_cannot_record_a_human_decision` returns `403 person_required`; `::a_human_decision_without_an_approved_human_gate_is_refused` refuses a missing, pending or agent-decided approval; `::a_pending_approval_cannot_gate_a_draft` refuses a pending gate.

entries.axis_b: A human decision cites the approval of its own gate

value.acceptance: OPEN — v1-t2-6: `ladder.record` passes `None` for the gate to `human_approved_gate_tx`, so any approved approval with a human approve decision on the same card qualifies. The check must compare `approval.gate` with the decision's gate.
OPEN — v1-t2-4: `ladder.evaluate` accepts an inline `options` array and records it with `option_set_version`; there is no authored option-set row the tenant versions independently of the request.

entries.axis_b: Questions are rows with fire_when, min_confidence and fail_policy

value.acceptance: OPEN — v1-t2-4: `decision_policy` carries kind, gate, threshold, fail_policy, action and meta; the question is an optional free string on the request, defaulted to the kind, and `fire_when`/`min_confidence` have no columns.

entries.axis_b: Publishing a refinement is a gated policy change

value.acceptance: OPEN — v1-t2-3: `refinements.publish` has `confirm = "none"`, writes the override and bumps the version with no approval; `decision_policies.update` is likewise ungated.

entries.axis_b: L1 asks the laya client and records its answer

value.acceptance: OPEN — v1-t2-2: no T2 path calls `POST /v1/systemone`; the answer and confidence are supplied by the caller, and `laya_configs` only pins model_ref, params and timeout.

entries.axis_b: An over-budget run is refused before the next call

value.acceptance: OPEN — v1-t2-5: no inference budget is declared or enforced in T2; the tree's only budget refusal is `429 tool_budget_exceeded`, not the §7.5 spelling `429 budget_exceeded`.

entries.axis_b: Tenant isolation on every ladder table

value.acceptance: the five decision tables are tenant-scoped with FORCE RLS as shipped by T0 in `migrations/0040_organisation.sql`; `migrations/0046_decision_ladder.sql` only adds columns, constraints and indexes, and both new indexes lead with `tenant_id`; the one-refinement and one-policy indexes are tenant-scoped.

artifacts.title: Requirements catalog — UI stack

entries.axis_b: interaction TTI, throttled, is the decision number

value.acceptance: CSR 5,426 ms (5,408–5,628) against SSR 5,736 ms (5,705–5,758), median n=5; both exceed 2 s so SSR's precondition is met, but SSR still loses the TTI comparison and the ranges do not overlap
value.requirement: navigationStart to the first drag that mutates list membership, 4× CPU and Slow 4G, median of five runs per stack

entries.axis_b: bundle size is reported gzip-9 with the raw size beside it

value.acceptance: CSR 290,723 B gzip-9 (809,797 B raw) against SSR 301,017 B gzip-9 (844,826 B raw); the 9,315,696 B SSR server binary is not shipped to the browser
value.requirement: sum the built site's wasm and js, gzip-9 each file, and record the raw total too

entries.axis_b: the 500-card first render is measured all-at-once and virtualised on both stacks

value.acceptance: CSR 4,726 ms all-at-once and 4,726 ms virtualised (240 cards); SSR 1,444 ms and 945 ms; SSR wins first paint and the win does not survive hydration
value.requirement: navigationStart to the 500th [data-card-id]; the all-at-once mode is the decision configuration and the virtualised mode is the fallback

entries.axis_b: drag frames over a 2 s pointer drag

value.acceptance: CSR p95 16.7 ms and 80.0% of frames at or below 16.7 ms; SSR p95 16.8 ms and 76.5%; both record zero long tasks over 50 ms, and the 95% threshold is missed by both stacks
value.requirement: rAF deltas plus longtask observation; pass is at least 95% of frames at or below 16.7 ms with no long task over 50 ms

entries.axis_b: SSE to DOM latency over 30 events

value.acceptance: CSR one run only: p50 1.0 ms and p95 1.8 ms; SSR not measured, because the five-run set did not complete inside the time-box
value.requirement: the fixture stamps the send time, the app marks the message and a MutationObserver marks the DOM change; report p50 and p95 against a p95 ceiling of 100 ms

entries.axis_b: a five-minute memory soak on both stacks

value.acceptance: not measured on either stack: the soak was skipped after the decision measurements closed
value.requirement: CDP Performance.getMetrics for JSHeapUsedSize plus Memory.getDOMCounters; more than 300 MB or more than 3× the card nodes is a signal

entries.axis_b: a release cold build from an empty target directory

value.acceptance: CSR 44.41 s (35.58–54.71, n=5, frontend only); SSR 56.54 s and 79.95 s (n=2, full server plus wasm); the 10-minute warning is not crossed
value.requirement: time the build from empty on both stacks; more than 10 minutes is a loop warning

entries.axis_b: auth is a pass or a forcing condition, not a latency race

value.acceptance: CSR passes 3/3 login to board to logout cycles with the token in memory; SSR passes 3/3; neither forces SSR, and CSR's authenticated SSE needs a fetch plus ReadableStream shim, recorded as work rather than a failure
value.requirement: run auth-code + PKCE S256 on CSR and HttpOnly session + CSRF on SSR; log out and in three times and deep-link while logged out

entries.axis_b: the ADR is the only durable artefact and the spike is deleted

value.acceptance: docs/decisions/0001-ui-stack.md is Accepted on 2026-11-08 with 16 measured rows; spikes/web is gone and apps/web is still absent
value.requirement: splice the measured table into the ADR before deleting spikes/web, and confirm apps/web is still absent

entries.axis_b: pair all 314 RM route decorators with their mount prefix

value.acceptance: the RM manifest carries 314 surfaces and appears exactly once each in parity.yaml
value.requirement: each method is paired with its path plus the mount prefix from src/routers/__init__.py and emitted as rm<TAB>METHOD /path

value.acceptance: the Planka manifest appears exactly once each in parity.yaml

entries.axis_b: enumerate the active n8n operation tuples and the four named flows

value.acceptance: the n8n manifest appears exactly once each in parity.yaml; the 280 card-type by list flows are one feature and are not rows

entries.axis_b: hold one row schema with no extra keys

value.acceptance: check-jsonschema --schemafile parity/schema.json parity/parity.yaml exits 0
value.requirement: parity/schema.json sets additionalProperties false and requires the nine keys id, app, area, surface, source, evidence, evidence_class, acceptance and status, with app in fr, rm, planka and n8n, evidence_class in A to E, and status in used, rare, unused and dropped

entries.axis_b: pass the executable gate G1 to G7

value.acceptance: the plan's §7 script exits 0 under bash with set -euo pipefail
value.requirement: ids are unique and match ^P-[0-9]{4}$; every used row carries an acceptance string; every surface appears exactly once; the count reconciles; two samples exist for B-class used; every dropped row starts decision: or replacement:

entries.axis_b: measure read-only, directly on the master

value.acceptance: the preflight in parity/evidence/00-preflight.txt records the disk and tool checks and the run reached the end
value.requirement: SQL runs on master as postgres, never through PgBouncer, never with a session SET; there is no prune and no state deletion; below 10 % disk the run stops and reports

entries.axis_b: sign the contract and update the ledger

value.acceptance: the SUMMARY carries the sign block; the rework note records the reconstituted lifecycle read back act by act
value.requirement: parity/SUMMARY.md carries signed_off with the reviewer, the date and the sha256 of parity.yaml, and the programme ledger row is updated

entries.axis_b: give every used id an acceptance string and only used ids

value.acceptance: gate G3 finds no used row without an acceptance string
value.requirement: acceptance is test:<crate>::<name>, e2e:<spec>::<name> or probe:<METHOD> <path>; no rare, unused or dropped row carries one

entries.axis_b: record the measurement as dated and not re-measurable

value.acceptance: the rework note records the residual and this pack repeats it without softening
value.requirement: the samples are dated 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-08; the live sources have moved on and no re-measurement is claimed

artifacts.change_initiative: The S04 action-registry rework (tranche 3, #526)

value.detail: fr's registry is the lesson: any projection reading a second source is the bug. S04 derives every projection from one ActionSpec.
value.objective: Remove the drift surface between HTTP, MCP, manifest and OpenAPI.

value.detail: Later slices add actions, never a surface.
value.objective: Replace 24 node packages and fr's 88 capability declarations with one registry.

value.detail: The gate covers the 16 internal actions plus the four fixtures.* external actions.
value.objective: 20 actions identical over HTTP and MCP.

value.detail: The attribute supplies name, version, kind, scopes, idempotent, timeout_ms, effect, confirm and tenancy.
value.objective: ActionSpec plus #[action] emit the spec value and an inventory::submit! from the same tokens.

value.detail: It fails on a duplicate name, an MCP-form collision, an MCP name outside the charset, a handler-less internal action or an unknown Scope.
value.objective: assert_registry_consistent runs in serve, worker and every test.

value.detail: One transaction writes the mutation, action_invocation and audit_event; S04 declares no events, so it writes no outbox row.
value.objective: Compose tenancy scope, idempotency claim, deadline and transaction around every call.

value.detail: Store spec and schema_hash; refuse a breaking refresh until conveyor admin actions approve <name> --version <n>.
value.objective: Ingest external OpenAPI operations as kind: external actions.

value.detail: A refused tool is absent, not noisy; an unresolvable tenant is 401 and a failed JWT bearer is never retried as a licence token.
value.objective: Serve MCP tools from the same Registry, scope-filtered.

artifacts.purpose: Record why S04 exists and what it must achieve: one declaration per invocable operation, from which manifest, OpenAPI operation, MCP tool and route are generated so HTTP and MCP cannot diverge.
artifacts.scope: S04 action registry slice. It replaces the 24 node packages and fr's 88 capability declarations; later slices add actions, never a surface. Domain actions (S05-S11), kind: workflow (S13), channel-mcp delivery rows (S06) and the signed mcp_server channel (S06-alpha) are out of scope.

entries.value: High-level work is decided in cross-department meetings; only the approval survives today.
Every decision that needed several positions carries those positions, conditions and dissent.
A meeting never weakens a gate; the stricter policy wins.
T19's §12 gate passes with a three-department majority, an inquorate deferral and a live owner decision.
Decision latency, agenda conversion, quorum-miss, commitment slippage and action closure recompute from rows.

entries.axis_b: an approval row records a decision but not the trade-offs, conditions, dissent and commitments around it
high-level programme, architecture, analysis and project work is decided between departments and needs their participation on the record
meetings become the decision forum over the four existing primitives, never a fifth unit and never a chat
each decision is arithmetic over typed positions and the linked approval's policy, not a summary written after the fact
close_item writes one approval_decision per qualifying seat with via='meeting' on every deciding item
an item whose required department is absent defers with reason inquorate and cannot be decided
a change of decision rule or participation is a new meeting_type version, never an edit of a pinned version
the owner decides one item live in the web room and one asynchronously over MCP, both recorded via='meeting'
a forum that produces no decision over a cycle is flagged and, on the owner's ruling, retired

entries.value: A policy change today has no route: the meeting type is versioned but only the schedule creates v1, and an inline policy is refused.

one live position per participant per item: stance (approve|approve_with_conditions|reject|abstain|request_evidence), rationale, conditions, optional commitment, surface and time; immutable once the item closes

minutes are a governed_asset(kind='minutes') drafted from the typed rows and published behind the chair's gate; dissent is kept verbatim and every action becomes a card

participant-hours derive from attendance and duration as the third D52 metering source; a meeting_type with no decision over a cycle is flagged for retirement
the /meetings console lists invitations and seats, the room with agenda, evidence, participants and live positions, the asynchronous queue, minutes and actions, and forum history and load

artifacts.title: Business capability map — T13 tool platform

value.detail: §11.1 definitions; §11.6 governed_asset(kind='tool_draft') then validation, security review, tools.publish and binding.
value.objective: Publish every callable operation as an immutable versioned toolkit.

value.detail: §11.1 distinguishes binding from grant; §11.4 says a binding's ceiling narrows only.
value.objective: Grant tenant-scoped access that narrows but never widens.

value.detail: §11.3; the executor's own knowledge and memory rungs are not tools, and a job that explicitly searches uses the retrieval toolkit.
value.objective: Reach job backends by one governed path.

value.detail: §11.4: read is audit-only; write is job authority plus audit; destructive needs approval, dry-run and dual control; spend needs a budget check and ledger.
value.objective: Gate read, write, destructive and spend appropriately.

value.detail: §11.3 step 3: additionalProperties false, enums, patterns and bounds, returning 422 tool_input_invalid.
value.objective: Refuse schema-invalid input before egress.

value.detail: §11.3 step 7; §11.9 per-tool calls, success rate, p95 latency, error classes and cost, plus per-job tool-budget usage.
value.objective: Make calls, cost and failures observable.

value.detail: §11.10: direct MinIO, mandatory tenant prefix, a content hash per object and a size cap; artifacts.list was migrated onto this store by #450.
value.objective: Store job bytes directly without a compatibility shim.

value.detail: §11.9: a tools.probe failure unbinds new runs with 409 tool_not_ready; a zero-call tool is flagged and retired (P10); schema drift opens a kata.
value.objective: Unbind unhealthy tools and retire unused ones.

entries.axis_b: 18 with ENABLE and FORCE row-level security

value.usage: every control-plane table carries tenant_id, ENABLE and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and the tenant policy, following the S03 convention; migrate twice must be idempotent (plan §6 step 2)

entries.axis_b: text plus CHECK, never CREATE TYPE

value.usage: channel_kind, delivery state, decision and decided_by_kind are text CHECK values in the migration and domain; no CREATE TYPE in 0005_control_plane.sql (S03 standard)

entries.axis_b: one conditional UPDATE with If-Match and a monotonic fence

value.usage: the claim binds the caller's If-Match to $5 and never reads a body version; zero rows is a refusal and a DB error is a refusal, never granted; claim_fence is monotonic so a holder past its TTL compares it before every write (plan §5.3, trap 5)

entries.axis_b: dedupe on (kind, dedupe_key) with a partial unique index

value.usage: the index covers pending and running only, so a dead job never blocks re-enqueue; handlers are idempotent on (kind, dedupe_key); every cadence is a schedule row, and `setInterval` is absent (plan §5.3, trap 4, property f)

entries.axis_b: one pending per gate; first-response-counts closes deliveries, not the gate

value.usage: decision and expiry race on WHERE status='pending' and the loser emits nothing; with required_decisions > 1 the gate stays pending after the first response while other recipients are closed as expired; approval.expire runs at 60 s (plan §5.4, trap 1, decision 5)

entries.axis_b: send outside the transaction with bounded retry and terminal-only retention

value.usage: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED plus lease_token; pending → sent → delivered | failed | expired; attempts >= max_attempts lands failed; backoff min(2^attempts · 5 s, 900 s); retention prunes terminal rows only (plan §5.6, trap 6)

entries.axis_b: in-transaction event row plus pg_notify over three topics

value.usage: the 17 event types of plan §5.6 write their row in the same transaction; run:{id}, approval:{id} and tenant are the topics; every mutation has exactly one write path (plan §5.6)

entries.axis_b: schedule rows under one advisory lock; three timers deleted

value.usage: periods are schedule rows under pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('conveyor:schedule')); 11 fr timers become job kinds; analytics-rollup, signup-onboarding-tick and workflows-cache are deleted, not ported (plan §5.3, decision 9)

POST /api/channels/telegram/{binding_id} checks the secret-token header, resolves (chat_id, topic_id) to channel_binding, tenant and sender, and calls approvals.decide or cards.comment; there is no per-channel decision path (plan §5.6)

entries.axis_b: worker-scraped andon gauge with a 1 s timeout

value.usage: conveyor_andon_engaged{tenant_id} and conveyor_andon_engaged_at_seconds are read from andon_state with a 1 s timeout; a dead exporter is an alarm via absent(), never a request-driven cache (plan §5.5)

entries.axis_b: state pauses the poller and refuses runs; never scales replicas

value.usage: andon.engage writes andon_state and emits andon.engaged; runs.create refuses 409 andon-engaged; the poller skips engaged tenants; release reverses both (plan §5.5, decision 6)

entries.axis_b: the plan §7 gate on port 8930; hosted preflight for the compile verdict

value.usage: the gate runs the six conveyor-api test binaries and the four conveyor-server binaries, asserts `rg 'setInterval' crates apps` is empty (property f), serves on [redacted-ip]:8930 and never port 8000; the compile/test verdict comes from the repository's GitHub-hosted preflight, with the local gate sub-second (plan §7)

artifacts.title: Technology Standards Catalog — S06 Control Plane (Phase D)

entries.axis_b: forced row-level security on every new table

value.usage: each S07 table carries tenant_id NOT NULL with ENABLE and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and the tenant_isolation policy using both USING and WITH CHECK, following S03's convention; quality_evaluation is append-only.

status, kind and verdict are text columns constrained by CHECK rather than native enums, so a new value is a migration, not an ALTER TYPE; governed_asset status is draft, in_review, approved or superseded.

entries.axis_b: a generated tsv with a literal english config

value.usage: the tsvector column names 'english' literally because current_setting is not immutable; ts_rank_cd must name the same configuration or it scores zero.

entries.axis_b: pg_trgm beside full text, never instead of it

value.usage: gin(title gin_trgm_ops) serves %, ILIKE and similarity(); tsv @@ tsquery needs gin(tsv); similarity ordering without a % predicate scans the table and is refused.

ts_match_vq and word_similarity_op must be LEAKPROOF or both GINs are dead under FORCE RLS; the plan records the 2026-11-08 measurement where the degraded plan satisfied a loose grep and the check was tightened.
revision.content_hash is the SHA-256 of the JCS-canonical post-mutation snapshot, so equal documents hash equally and a diff is over content, not storage order.
all 32 operations are registry-declared actions with unversioned host routes; the durable name is the action, and RM's unprefixed mounts get no alias or rewrite.

entries.axis_b: one event per mutation in the transaction

value.usage: eleven internal event types are written in the mutation's transaction; event names are internal vocabulary and no consumer's naming is copied into the schema.

entries.axis_b: quality scoring outside the mutation lock

value.usage: quality.score runs as job(kind='quality.score', dedupe_key='revision:<id>') after commit; several trigram queries inside the mutation would hold the asset row lock, which the plan refuses.
the three search weights are one constant tuned by a bounded grid search, not a learned model; pgvector ships only on the §5.6 trigger.

artifacts.title: Architecture Requirement Catalogue — SPEC-V2 (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

artifacts.change_initiative: The conveyor programme's ADM capability adoption (T9)

entries.axis_b: One model, one store, one action registry

value.evidence: crates/actions/src/lib.rs; migrations/*.sql; crates/actions/tests/registry.rs
value.implications: A new capability is a table plus actions in this workspace, not a new service; no feature keeps a private file or cache as its record of truth.
value.rationale: The estate's pain is distributed fragments of one model; one registry makes permission, audit and replay uniform, and its exact set is asserted by its own test.
value.statement: A programme, its projects, their work, their decisions and their evidence are rows in one Postgres database written through one action registry; a concept has one table and one set of actions.

entries.axis_b: Every mutation is an action; the database is not the API

value.evidence: crates/actions/src/invoke.rs; the registry test committed_action_dump_matches_the_registry
value.implications: A new write is an action with a schema, a scope and a test; a read-only probe is BEGIN READ ONLY.
value.rationale: RFC 9457 errors, If-Match/_version preconditions, revision history and audit hang off the action envelope; a SQL write bypasses every one of them.
value.statement: A write goes through an action with its scope, tenant, precondition and event; no handler, UI or script writes rows by SQL.

entries.axis_b: Tenant isolation is structural, not a filter

value.evidence: crates/store/src/scope.rs; crates/actions/tests/registry.rs a_foreign_tenant_parent_id_resolves_to_404_never_to_a_write
value.implications: A new table ships with its policy in the same migration and a foreign-tenant 404 test; a session-level GUC through a pooler is forbidden.
value.rationale: The store's begin_scoped is the only path that sets the tenant GUC; a filtered query is one forgotten predicate away from a leak.
value.statement: Every tenant-owned table has RLS enabled and forced, and every query runs under the tenant's scope; a cross-tenant id resolves to 404.

entries.axis_b: Publication is a decision, never a side effect

value.evidence: crates/actions/src/documents/revisions.rs; crates/render/src/markdown.rs
value.implications: A new public surface filters on the public bit and carries the tenant; preview uses the same renderer as the public page.
value.rationale: The executor never approves its own work; documents.publish is the only action that moves the public bit, and the renderer neutralises raw HTML.
value.statement: A row is public only when an admin's publish decision makes it public; an author's write never publishes and author markup is never executable on the public page.

entries.axis_b: Every output is versioned, attributable and reversible

value.evidence: migrations/0042_document_workflow.sql; crates/store/src/document.rs
value.implications: A new aggregate that holds work products reuses the document model or carries the same provenance; deletion is a tombstone.
value.rationale: The programme is judged on its intermediate work products; an output a reviewer cannot trace to author, version and evidence is not auditable.
value.statement: A text output carries its author, a content hash and a revision history; every edit is versioned and a restore copies a version forward.

entries.axis_b: Programme truth is computed, never hand-written

value.evidence: scripts/build-coverage.py; scripts/build-programme-seed.py; scripts/check-output-standard.py
value.implications: A new programme fact gets a generator and a --check gate; a document may explain the truth but may not be its only home.
value.rationale: A hand-written status is the first thing to rot; the standard generates every project's expected set and the pack is built from the tree.
value.statement: A project's status, units, dependencies and expected outputs come from measured sources and are regenerated by scripts; a checklist is derived from the standard.

entries.axis_b: Gates refuse; a gate that never refuses is broken

value.evidence: crates/actions/tests/authoring_standard.rs; the 409 blocked_by gate in crates/actions/src/programme.rs
value.implications: A gate names what is missing and offers the next step; a refusal is covered at the boundary the caller uses.
value.rationale: The programme's publish and dependency gates exist because a publish without evidence happened; a refusal is the product, not an error path.
value.statement: A quality gate is a refusal with an actionable reason, exercised by a test that proves the refusal; a gate that never refused in a full cycle is treated as broken.

value.evidence: migrations/0044_plan_spine.sql; crates/actions/tests/plan_spine.rs
value.implications: A project's inception names its dependencies and the contract it sits under; a deviation is a decision record.
value.rationale: Untyped coupling hides the order the programme actually needs; the gate answers 409 blocked_by naming the open dependency.
value.statement: A dependency between projects is typed and the programme gate enforces the blocking kind; a tranche review is a programme decision on evidence.

value.evidence: crates/actions/src/documents/secrets.rs; scripts/ci/no-private-refs.sh
value.implications: A credential is referenced, never printed; a public output and the snapshot are scanned before publication.
value.rationale: The repository is public, so a leak is permanent; the secret aggregate stores only a sealed form.
value.statement: A secret is write-only; no action returns its value, and no secret, token or private host enters the public repository or a published output.

entries.axis_b: The estate is one deployable service per concept, absorbed not duplicated

value.evidence: docs/decisions/0005-absorption-sequence-and-repo-scope.md; crates/actions/src/ops/
value.implications: A new integration adds an action and a client in this workspace; a retired service's data is migrated, not forked.
value.rationale: ADR 0005 fixes the absorption sequence; the public repository cannot carry a hidden dependency on a private host.
value.statement: A service the organisation depends on is either this workspace's own code or an absorbed, contract-tested module behind an action; a second deployment of the same concept is retired.

board.charter: The board governs the conveyor programme's architecture. It adopts the principles catalogue and the tailored ADM profile, approves architecture contracts, and accepts or rejects waivers. It cannot approve a gate it requested and cannot waive a deviation it owns. It meets at each tranche review and on a contract request. Quorum: the chair. Every decision is recorded with the evidence it was taken on.

compliance_reviews.findings: This retrospective Phase-G review records the level compliant for the record set it assesses under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14; the operations delivery was executed and merged, but no contemporaneous lifecycle review exists, and that absence is carried as the project's open record item rather than as non-conformance. At the 2026-11-27 snapshot the project row is active at version 12 (track v2, ADM phase G, capability plateau, tranche 5) with meta.measured_status built; it carries a scope baseline and a charter but no contract, Phase A–D artefact set, Phase-G review or closure evidence. The delivery evidence is PR #438 (the incident lifecycle, the four write verbs and the postmortem) and PR #434 (the /operations console), plus docs/evidence/record/evidence/T7-acceptance.md: 31 tests pass on 2026-11-24 and the clause map covers every §12 T7 clause. The two P1 findings the fresh snapshot found unresolved are fixed at ca155fada: v1-w1b-4 (dual control and a recorded dry run at the invoke boundary) and v1-w3a-5 (a no-action mitigation that lets a zero-write incident be postmortemed and resolved); their tests are in destructive_gate.rs, ops.rs and ops_write.rs. The live cluster proof scripts/ops-live-proof.sh did not run: the operator CLI is absent on this box and the deployed conveyor was older than the lane. The manifest's gate is the executed suite, as T7-acceptance.md states; the live clause is carried as a deploy-bound open item, not rounded up. The seed says closed and the record is active; this rework closes the project through the one gate, which resolves the seed/live drift. The residual v1-u5-copilot-gate-quorum finding remains S10's, not T7's. This content supplies the seven A–D artefacts, the charter, the Statement of Architecture Work, the delivery contract, this review, the project-brief/evidence outputs and the closure review. A non-conformant level would require a waiver the programme forbids; the honest residue is the deploy-bound live proof and the S10 finding.

At the 2026-11-27 snapshot the project row is status closed at version 12 (track v2, ADM phase G, capability plateau, tranche 5) with meta.measured_status built and issues #87, #629 and #655 linked; before this run it had no charter, no Statement of Architecture Work, no delivery contract, no Phase A–D artefact set, no Phase-G compliance review and no gate receipt. A non-conformant level would require a waiver the programme forbids; the honest residue is the two named risks.
