This retrospective Phase-G review records the compliance level non_conformant for T2 under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. It names the six findings this batch admitted, each by id and by what is missing. v1-t2-1 (P0) — a generated draft can be attached by `documents.compose` with no gate: the action accepts `card_id` and `meta.generated = true` and writes an attached, active document; the `draft.apply` gate exists only in `ladder.apply_draft` and the generated-class refusal only in `documents.update`, so the create path bypasses both. This finding blocks closure of the fourth §12 clause, "a generated draft cannot transition a card", and therefore blocks closure of T2. v1-t2-2 — L1 never calls laya: `ladder.evaluate` records the `answer`, `confidence`, `probabilities` and `latency_ms` supplied by its caller; `laya_configs` pins model_ref, params and timeout_ms, but no T2 path issues `POST /v1/systemone`, so the recorded L1 decision is a shape, not an inference. v1-t2-3 — `refinements.publish` is ungated: the action writes the tenant's threshold, rule and fail-action override and bumps its version with `confirm = "none"` and no approval, although §7.2 calls a refinement change a gated policy change; `decision_policies.update` is likewise ungated. v1-t2-4 — options and questions are inline free text: `ladder.evaluate` accepts an `options` array of key/label/payload objects and a free `question` string in the request, and `decision_policy` carries kind, gate, threshold, fail_policy and action but no authored question, `fire_when` or `min_confidence`, so §7.2's "options are rows, questions are rows" is not met. v1-t2-5 — budget code spelling: §7.5 records `429 budget_exceeded`, but T2 enforces no inference budget and the only budget refusal in the tree is the tool-spend `429 tool_budget_exceeded` in `crates/actions/src/invoke.rs` and `crates/actions/src/broker.rs` (#526), so the documented slug has no implementation. v1-t2-6 — a human decision cites any approved approval, not its gate: `ladder.record` calls `human_approved_gate_tx(..., None, card_id)`, so the `gate` it was given is never compared with `approval.gate`; only `ladder.apply_draft` passes `Some(DRAFT_APPLY_GATE)`, and a `gate.precheck` decision can cite an approval for a different gate on the same card. The delivered clauses are proved by named tests: `decision_ladder.rs::a_rule_a_laya_and_a_human_decision_share_one_audit_shape`, `::a_refinement_changes_a_threshold_without_a_code_change`, `::every_decision_pins_the_refinement_and_laya_config_versions` and, on the apply/update paths, `::a_generated_draft_cannot_transition_a_card`, with `ladder_human_gate.rs::a_service_principal_cannot_record_a_human_decision`, `::a_human_decision_without_an_approved_human_gate_is_refused`, `::a_pending_approval_cannot_gate_a_draft` and `::a_human_draft_apply_decision_and_approval_applies_the_draft`. The close also carried a mandatory_artefacts gap: at the 2026-11-21T19:24:46Z rework snapshot the seven Phase A–D artefacts, the Statement of Architecture Work and the delivery contract were absent; this rework produces and publishes stakeholder_map, driver_goal_objective, requirements_catalog and solution_concept (Phase A), business_capability_map (Phase B), data_entity_catalog (Phase C) and technology_standards (Phase D), and records this review. No original Phase-G review existed; this one is retrospective and does not attest contemporaneous intent.

Dispositions at this review. v1-t2-1 is FIXED: `documents.compose` now derives the generated class from the request's attribution and stamps `meta.generated` server-side, so a caller cannot unset it, and a `card_id` on a generated draft is refused `409 draft_requires_gate`; proved at `920a1dcbfa6427b59aada92a63b6c29eb6bdcde6` by `crates/actions/tests/documents_compose_gate.rs` (4/4) with `process_step` (20/20). The P0 that blocked closure is therefore lifted and the ledger carries it resolved. v1-t2-3 (`refinements.publish` ungated) and v1-t2-6 (a human decision cites any approved approval) remain open P1 packages owned by T2 and scheduled behind this batch; v1-t2-5 is a P2 correction. Under this programme's manifest the product gate is P0-only, so the two P1s do not block closure, and they are carried as packages rather than waived.

compliance_reviews.findings: This retrospective Phase-G review records the compliance level non_conformant for T4 under the standing delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`. It names the four findings this batch admitted, each by id and by what is missing. v1-p6-2 (P1) — the systemic path terminates at a process-run id: `coach.rs:994-999` starts `KATA_PROCESS` with `{interruption_id}` and stores the run id as `kata_candidate_id`; there is no kata record naming an instrument and success threshold, no tenant-kata scoping, no measurement and no adoption gate, so a systemic finding never changes production. v1-p6-4 (P1) — interruptions are silently dropped: the cap counts every interruption on a card regardless of signature (`count_interruptions_for_card_tx`, line 603), refuses the fourth failed run at `COACH_INTERRUPTION_MAX` (line 608) with no coach card and no escalation, and `board/pull.rs:359` suppresses coaching whenever any live root run exists on the card. v1-p6-5 (P1) — the coach is wired only to failed runs: `coach.interrupt` has one caller, `err.card` (`board/pull.rs:424`); WIP breaches, stale leases, gate timeouts and board events, all section 6.2 inputs, have no producer. v1-p6-6 (P2) — orphan coach cards can be created by the public create path: `board/cards.rs:104` accepts any catalogue card type, including coach, and validates neither an interruption row nor `meta.interrupted_card_id`. Clause dispositions. Clause 2 is proved by `coach.rs::a_repeat_signature_escalates_instead_of_a_second_card` (line 683) and clause 3 by `::a_failed_coach_run_never_opens_a_coach_card` (line 745) with `::a_nested_coach_run_is_refused` (line 1343). Clause 1 has a named passing test for a first interruption (`::an_interruption_yields_one_coach_card_one_triage_and_one_remedy`, line 577) but is refuted as a universal by v1-p6-4, so it is not proved at HEAD. Clause 4 has a named passing test (`::a_systemic_class_opens_one_kata`, line 816, with `::a_transient_class_opens_no_kata`, line 864) but proves only a process start; v1-p6-2 shows the kata record, instrument and threshold that the clause intends are absent, so the clause is proved only in the weaker sense. The close also carried a mandatory_artefacts gap: at the 2026-11-22 rework snapshot the seven Phase A–D artefacts, the Statement of Architecture Work and the delivery contract were absent; this rework produces and publishes stakeholder_map, driver_goal_objective, requirements_catalog and solution_concept (Phase A), business_capability_map (Phase B), data_entity_catalog (Phase C) and technology_standards (Phase D), and records this review. No original Phase-G review existed; this one is retrospective and does not attest contemporaneous intent. The register's `closed` status is retained because no open finding is P0 and the manifest's product gate is P0-only; v1-p6-2, v1-p6-4 and v1-p6-5 are carried as P1 packages and v1-p6-6 as P2, none waived.

This retrospective Phase-G review records the compliance level compliant for T13 under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. It names the five findings this batch admitted and what each leaves undone.

T13-R1 — The six gate proofs exist as named tests in crates/actions/tests/tool_platform.rs, but no gate-run output is recorded. Acceptance is evidenced by source, not by a passing run.
T13-R2 — The tests insert tool, toolkit and tool_binding rows directly; the header states the slice ships no catalogue actions and the estate import is T14. Gap ledger v1-p111-1 also says the tool binding has no writer, so a bound job is proved with a seeded binding, not a production binding path.
T13-R3 — The destructive test proves only the missing-approval refusal (403 approval_required, zero destination hits, no ledger row). It does not evidence the approval, dry-run and dual-control execution path §11.4 requires.
T13-R4 — The round-trip test uses the in-memory store that Pg::fresh configures when no endpoint is set, and gap ledger v1-p1110-1 says JobStorage is test-only. No live MinIO path is evidenced.
T13-R5 — The §12 row's coding toolkit and one kag-era toolkit plus V1 external-action migration is only partly evidenced: the tests use a coding fixture and a fixtures toolkit, and exercise no kag-era toolkit or V1 migration. Long operations, redaction, output_schema and BYO are open in the ledger (v1-w4a-5, v1-p111-3, v1-p118-2, v1-w4a-6).

The proving suite was re-run at the lane head for this review: tool_platform 17/17 passed at lane head 582e2dc6 (2026-11-22): the six §12 gate proofs plus the ceiling, write-verification, idempotency and sealed-credential tests, against a fresh Postgres 18 and a counting HTTP stub. The six §12 clauses are therefore evidenced by a passing wire-level suite, not only by source; the findings above are carried as named deviations and the closure is withheld until they are executed or waived.

This retrospective Phase-G review records the compliance level non_conformant for T2 under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. It names the six findings this batch admitted, each by id and by what is missing. v1-t2-1 (P0) — a generated draft can be attached by `documents.compose` with no gate: the action accepts `card_id` and `meta.generated = true` and writes an attached, active document; the `draft.apply` gate exists only in `ladder.apply_draft` and the generated-class refusal only in `documents.update`, so the create path bypasses both. This finding blocks closure of the fourth §12 clause, "a generated draft cannot transition a card", and therefore blocks closure of T2. v1-t2-2 — L1 never calls laya: `ladder.evaluate` records the `answer`, `confidence`, `probabilities` and `latency_ms` supplied by its caller; `laya_configs` pins model_ref, params and timeout_ms, but no T2 path issues `POST /v1/systemone`, so the recorded L1 decision is a shape, not an inference. v1-t2-3 — `refinements.publish` is ungated: the action writes the tenant's threshold, rule and fail-action override and bumps its version with `confirm = "none"` and no approval, although §7.2 calls a refinement change a gated policy change; `decision_policies.update` is likewise ungated. v1-t2-4 — options and questions are inline free text: `ladder.evaluate` accepts an `options` array of key/label/payload objects and a free `question` string in the request, and `decision_policy` carries kind, gate, threshold, fail_policy and action but no authored question, `fire_when` or `min_confidence`, so §7.2's "options are rows, questions are rows" is not met. v1-t2-5 — budget code spelling: §7.5 records `429 budget_exceeded`, but T2 enforces no inference budget and the only budget refusal in the tree is the tool-spend `429 tool_budget_exceeded` in `crates/actions/src/invoke.rs` and `crates/actions/src/broker.rs` (#526), so the documented slug has no implementation. v1-t2-6 — a human decision cites any approved approval, not its gate: `ladder.record` calls `human_approved_gate_tx(..., None, card_id)`, so the `gate` it was given is never compared with `approval.gate`; only `ladder.apply_draft` passes `Some(DRAFT_APPLY_GATE)`, and a `gate.precheck` decision can cite an approval for a different gate on the same card. The delivered clauses are proved by named tests: `decision_ladder.rs::a_rule_a_laya_and_a_human_decision_share_one_audit_shape`, `::a_refinement_changes_a_threshold_without_a_code_change`, `::every_decision_pins_the_refinement_and_laya_config_versions` and, on the apply/update paths, `::a_generated_draft_cannot_transition_a_card`, with `ladder_human_gate.rs::a_service_principal_cannot_record_a_human_decision`, `::a_human_decision_without_an_approved_human_gate_is_refused`, `::a_pending_approval_cannot_gate_a_draft` and `::a_human_draft_apply_decision_and_approval_applies_the_draft`. The close also carried a mandatory_artefacts gap: at the 2026-11-21T19:24:46Z rework snapshot the seven Phase A–D artefacts, the Statement of Architecture Work and the delivery contract were absent; this rework produces and publishes stakeholder_map, driver_goal_objective, requirements_catalog and solution_concept (Phase A), business_capability_map (Phase B), data_entity_catalog (Phase C) and technology_standards (Phase D), and records this review. No original Phase-G review existed; this one is retrospective and does not attest contemporaneous intent.

Dispositions at this review. v1-t2-1 is FIXED: `documents.compose` now derives the generated class from the request's attribution and stamps `meta.generated` server-side, so a caller cannot unset it, and a `card_id` on a generated draft is refused `409 draft_requires_gate`; proved at `920a1dcbfa6427b59aada92a63b6c29eb6bdcde6` by `crates/actions/tests/documents_compose_gate.rs` (4/4) with `process_step` (20/20). The P0 that blocked closure is therefore lifted and the ledger carries it resolved. v1-t2-3 (`refinements.publish` ungated) and v1-t2-6 (a human decision cites any approved approval) remain open P1 packages owned by T2 and scheduled behind this batch; v1-t2-5 is a P2 correction. Under this programme's manifest the product gate is P0-only, so the two P1s do not block closure, and they are carried as packages rather than waived.

contracts.body:
# Statement of Architecture Work — T13 Tool platform

## Context
SPEC_V2 §11 replaces ad-hoc backend calls with one governed path. The conveyor already owns actions, secrets, entitlements, audit and a durable queue, so a second catalogue/queue/runner (the predecessor MCP server) is refused (D44, D59). T13 is the slice that makes the one path real.

## Scope
The broker `tools.call` and its seven steps; the four catalogue/ledger tables; effect-class gating; the closed-schema input check; credential aliases over sealed secrets; the direct MinIO storage adapter with the mandatory tenant prefix; the coding toolkit and one kag-era toolkit; V1 external-action migration; six gate proofs.

## Approach
Implement the broker and storage layers in the conveyor workspace, prove each refusal before dispatch at the wire (a counting stub), record one `tool_call` and one `tool.called` event per call, and record every artefact of this rework retrospectively from §11 and the tests rather than from memory.

## Deliverables
`crates/actions/tests/tool_platform.rs` (the six proofs and the extra broker tests); `conveyor_actions::storage::{JobStorage, TENANT_PREFIX, sha256_hex}`; `conveyor_store::tool::{calls_for_run, ToolCallRow}`; `conveyor_actions::prompt::compile_for_audit`; the reused `conveyor_store::secret::create_secret_tx`; tables `tool`, `toolkit`, `tool_binding`, `tool_call`; action `tools.call`; event `tool.called`.

## Constraints and standards
Rust workspace; PostgreSQL 18; MinIO (S3-compatible) as the platform store; a closed JSON-Schema subset (additionalProperties false, enums, patterns, bounds); OpenAPI 3.1 and streamable-HTTP MCP as the only two BYO forms; idempotency keys on writes and bounded polls.

## Acceptance
The six §12 clauses and their named tests, as written in `acceptance/programme/T13.toml`; the manifest is the gate, not this document.

## Risks
The suite serialises because the destination URL is process-global; the storage test path is test-only until live MinIO wiring exists; the catalogue write path is deferred to T14; a production binding writer is still absent.

## Decisions closed by this rework
The binding row is the broker's authority; refusals are proved on the wire; `tool_call` is not `action_invocation`; the storage adapter builds every key, so traversal and hash mismatches are refused.

Clauses 2, 3 and 5 are proved by named tests; clause 1 is proved for a project backlog and not for the programme-wide backlog (v1-p82-5); clause 4 is unproved at HEAD because free-text placeholders satisfy the evidence check (v1-p83-1) and the baseline requirement is not gated (v1-p83-4). contracts.body:
# Delivery contract — T13 Tool platform (retrospective, 2026-11-22)

**Scope.** IN: the broker tools.call; tool, toolkit, tool_binding and tool_call; effect classes read/write/destructive/spend; binding-scoped credential aliases over sealed secrets; the direct MinIO storage adapter with the tenant prefix; the coding toolkit and one kag-era toolkit; V1's external actions migrated onto toolkit operations and artifacts.list onto the storage adapter; the six T13 gate proofs. OUT: catalogue actions and the estate import (T14); the agent platform gateway nonagenticai_mcp_server (D44/D59); BYO publication surface (gap ledger v1-w4a-6); live MinIO wiring (v1-p1110-1); a production tool_binding writer (v1-p111-1).

**Assignment.** Project T13 "Tool platform", issue #76, depends on T2, spec SPEC_V2 §11.1-§11.10, SPEC_V2 §12 T13, plan status authorised (tranche 3).

**Acceptance criteria.** The §12 gate, per clause:

a. A development job calls coding through the broker, not nonagenticai_mcp_server. *Proof:* a_bound_job_calls_coding_through_the_broker: 200; exactly one stub hit; output path /api/jobs via the registered coding destination alias.
b. A tool_call is recorded. *Proof:* one_call_is_one_ledger_row: exactly one row for one call, tool_key coding.jobs.create, toolkit version 1, status ok, http_status 200, 64-hex sha256 input hash, latency; exactly one tool.called event.
c. A destructive call without the tenant's configured approvals is refused. *Proof:* a_destructive_call_without_approvals_is_refused: 403 approval_required; zero destination hits; no tool_call row.
d. Schema-invalid input is refused before the backend call. *Proof:* a_closed_schema_refuses_before_the_call: 422 tool_input_invalid with populated errors[] for an undeclared property, a pattern violation and a numeric bound; zero destination hits; a valid document returns 200 and reaches the destination.
e. A job writes and reads a tenant-prefixed object. *Proof:* a_job_round_trips_a_tenant_prefixed_object: key starts tenant/<tenant_id>/; sha256 matches; read-back bytes match; a wrong hash is refused; head finds the object; a traversal name is refused.
f. The compiled prompt carries no S3 key. *Proof:* the_compiled_prompt_carries_no_s3_key: compiled copilot_system@1 contains none of the access-key, secret-key or CONVEYOR_S3_ sentinels.

**Responsibilities.**

- **T13 delivery** — Ship the broker tools.call, the four catalogue/ledger tables, credential-alias resolution, the tenant-prefixed storage adapter and the proving tests.
- **T2** — Supplies the run and durable-queue context; tool_binding.run_id targets a run, and §12 places T13 after T2.
- **T14** — Owns the estate import; this slice ships no catalogue actions, per the test header.
- **Coding fleet owner** — Registers and reviews the coding destination alias; no caller-supplied URL is admitted at call time (§11.3 step 5).
- **Tenant admins** — Configure destructive-call approvals (§11.4) and approve BYO toolkit publication (§11.5).
- **Platform operator** — Publishes immutable versions, runs tools.probe and retires zero-call tools (§11.6, §11.9).

**Manifest.** The storage, tool and prompt entries are symbol references read from the tests, not independently opened file paths. No migration filename or source pin is asserted because none was read. Adds tables tool, toolkit, tool_binding, tool_call; action tools.call; event tool.called.

**Retrospective.** Authored from §11 and the six proving tests; no gate run is recorded in this record. The tests write tool rows directly because the slice ships no catalogue actions. Decisions closed: the binding row is the broker's authority; refusals are asserted on the wire through the stub counter; tool_call is not action_invocation; the storage adapter builds every key, so traversal names and hash mismatches are refused. Traps to carry: the destination URL is process-global, so the suite serialises; the storage test uses the in-memory store when no endpoint is configured; a production binding writer and the estate import remain outside this slice.
